prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S183: East Tube Dispatch Console maintains the approved route map and the current availability status of supported pneumatic segments.
S184: East Tube Dispatch Console checks the selected route against the destination cabinet, current network availability, and approved routing configuration before releasing a capsule.
S185: The console confirms that the destination is reachable and that the route does not include a segment reported unavailable.
S186: Route selection uses the destination identifier and the latest approved configuration version rather than an operator-entered sequence of segments.
S187: Before dispatch, the console checks for conflicting capsule movements and confirms that required interlocks are satisfied.
S188: The Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status, transfer progress, and delivery confirmation to the dispatch console.
S189: If route status is stale or incomplete, the console holds the capsule and displays the condition for operator review.
S190: A loss of communication with a route sensor prevents the console from treating the affected segment as available.
S191: An interruption during transit is recorded with the capsule identifier, last confirmed location, and time of the interruption.
S192: The console alerts a Pharmacy Technician when a transfer stops progressing or cannot be confirmed at its destination.
S193: After recovery, the console requires refreshed segment status and an approved route decision before dispatch resumes.
S194: Route and temperature records retain timestamps and equipment identifiers to support operational review and investigation.
S195: The Pharmacy Verification Station serves as the final controlled checkpoint before a medication is made available for dispensing.
S196: The Clinical Pharmacist compares the active medication order with the product, strength, dosage form, dose, route, and scheduled time.
S197: The Clinical Pharmacist also confirms that the patient identifiers and pharmacy label agree with the authorized order.
S198: The Pharmacy Technician checks package integrity, lot identification, and expiry before presenting the medication for verification.
S199: For designated high-risk medications, an independent second check is completed and recorded before authorization.
S200: Any mismatch places the medication on hold until the discrepancy is resolved by an authorized pharmacy professional.
S201: The verification record captures the approving staff identity, time, and medication identifiers for later review.
S202: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot remains inhibited from completing a dispense until the required pharmacy authorization is present.
S203: The Clinical Pharmacist resolves unclear or conflicting order details through the Medication Order Gateway before authorizing release.
S204: The South Ward Cabinet Controller receives the release note and applies its own approved cabinet configuration before enabling any compartment.
